translation_en: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whenever a Muslim plants a tree, whatever is eaten from it is charity for him; whatever is stolen from it is charity; whatever a wild animal eats from it is charity; whatever birds eat is charity; and whatever anyone takes from it is charity for him.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Prophet entered the date orchard of Umm Mubashshir al-Ansariyyah and asked her, “Who planted these date palms, a Muslim or a disbeliever?” She said, “A Muslim.” He said: “A Muslim does not plant a tree or sow a crop from which a person, animal, or anything else eats, without it being charity for him.”

Muhammad ibn Hatim and Ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “A Muslim man does not plant a tree or sow a crop from which a wild animal, bird, or anything else eats without earning reward for it.” Ibn Abi Khalaf’s wording says, “a bird or anything.”

Ahmad ibn Sa‘id ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah narrated to us: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us: ‘Amr ibn Dinar informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: The Prophet entered a garden belonging to Umm Ma‘bad and asked, “O Umm Ma‘bad, who planted these date palms, a Muslim or a disbeliever?” She said, “A Muslim.” He said: “A Muslim does not plant a tree from which a person, animal, or bird eats without it being charity for him until the Day of Resurrection.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us; Abu Kurayb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Abu Mu‘awiyah; ‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: ‘Ammar ibn Muhammad narrated to us; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us. All reported from al-A‘mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir. ‘Amr’s report from ‘Ammar and Abu Kurayb’s report from Abu Mu‘awiyah add “from Umm Mubashshir”; Ibn Fudayl’s report says “from the wife of Zayd ibn Harithah.” Ishaq’s report from Abu Mu‘awiyah sometimes says “from Umm Mubashshir,” and sometimes omits it. All of them report from the Prophet a report like ‘Ata’, Abu al-Zubayr, and ‘Amr ibn Dinar.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id, and Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya’s. Yahya said: Abu ‘Awanah informed us; the other two said: Abu ‘Awanah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whenever a Muslim plants a tree or sows a crop, and a bird, person, or animal eats from it, it is charity for him.”

‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Aban ibn Yazid narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik said that the Prophet of Allah entered the date orchard of Umm Mubashshir, a woman from the Ansar, and asked: “Who planted these date palms, a Muslim or a disbeliever?” They said, “A Muslim,” and he related a report like theirs.

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, that Abu al-Zubayr informed him from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah said: “If you sell fruit to your brother…” Muhammad ibn ‘Abbad narrated to us: Abu Damrah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, who heard Jabir say the Messenger of Allah said: “If you sell fruit to your brother and it is struck by a calamity, it is not lawful for you to take anything from him. Why would you take your brother’s property without right?”
Al-Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to us: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, with this chain and a report like it.

Bishr ibn al-Hakam, Ibrahim ibn Dinar, and ‘Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-‘Ala’ narrated to us—and the wording is Bishr’s. They said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A‘raj, from Sulayman ibn ‘Atiq, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah ordered compensation for crop calamities. Abu Ishaq, Muslim’s companion, said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to us from Sufyan with this report.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, that the Prophet forbade selling dates until they had ripened. We asked Anas what ripening meant. He said, “They turn red and yellow.” He added: “If Allah prevents the fruit from growing, by what right would you take your brother’s property?”

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed me: Malik informed me, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah forbade selling fruit until it ripened. They asked what ripening meant, and he said, “It turns red.” He said: “If Allah prevents the fruit, by what right would you take your brother’s property?”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abbad narrated to me: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, that the Prophet said: “If Allah does not make it bear fruit, by what right would one of you take his brother’s property?”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Bukayr, from ‘Iyad ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said: A man suffered a loss on fruit he had bought during the Messenger of Allah’s time, and his debt became large. The Messenger of Allah said: “Give charity to him.” People gave charity, but it did not cover his debt. The Messenger of Allah said to his creditors: “Take what you find; you have no claim beyond that.”
Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-A‘la informed me: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: ‘Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, with this chain and a report like it.

More than one of our companions narrated to me: Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us: my brother narrated to me, from Sulayman, Ibn Bilal, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Abu al-Rijal Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, that his mother ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman said: I heard ‘Aishah say: The Messenger of Allah heard two disputants at the door, their voices raised. One was asking the other to reduce his debt and be lenient in some matter, while the other said, “By Allah, I will not do it.” The Messenger of Allah came out and said: “Where is the one who swore by Allah not to do a good deed?” The man said, “It is I, Messenger of Allah. He may have whichever of those he prefers.”

Harmalah ibn Yahya informed us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who told me that ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik informed him from his father: During the Messenger of Allah’s time, I demanded in the mosque a debt owed to me by Ibn Abi Hadrad. Our voices rose until the Messenger of Allah heard us while in his house. He came out, drew aside the curtain of his room, and called to Ka‘b ibn Malik, “O Ka‘b!” He answered, “At your service, Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet gestured with his hand for him to remit half of the debt. Ka‘b said, “I have done so, Messenger of Allah.” The Messenger said: “Stand and settle it.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar informed us: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, that Ka‘b ibn Malik told him he demanded a debt owed to him by Ibn Abi Hadrad, with a report like Ibn Wahb’s.

Muslim said: Al-Layth ibn Sa‘d narrated to me: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah narrated to me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, from Ka‘b ibn Malik, who had a debt owed by ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami. He met him and pressed him for it. They spoke until their voices rose. The Messenger of Allah passed by and said, “O Ka‘b,” then gestured with his hand as if to say, “Half.” Ka‘b took half of what was owed and left the other half.

Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm informed me that ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz told him that Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah say the Messenger of Allah—or I heard the Messenger say: “Whoever finds his own property with a man who has become bankrupt, or a person who has become bankrupt, has more right to it than anyone else.”

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Hushaym informed us; Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn Rumh both reported from al-Layth ibn Sa‘d; Abu al-Rabi‘ and Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Hammad, Ibn Zayd, narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab, Yahya ibn Sa‘id, and Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us. All reported with this chain, with the meaning of Zuhayr’s hadith. Ibn Rumh alone says in his version, “Any person who becomes bankrupt.”

Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sulayman, Ibn ‘Ikrimah ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi, narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Ibn Abi Husayn told me that Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm informed him that ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, regarding a man who becomes insolvent and the merchandise is found with him intact and undistributed: “It belongs to the person who sold it to him.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “If a man becomes bankrupt and another man finds his own goods intact with him, he has more right to them.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Sa‘id narrated to us; and Zuhayr narrated to me: Mu‘adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to me. Both reported from Qatadah with this chain and a report like it, saying: “He has more right to it than the creditors.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha‘ir narrated to me: Abu Salamah al-Khuza‘i narrated to us—Hajjaj said it was Mansur ibn Salamah: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, from Khuthaym ibn ‘Irak, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “If a man becomes bankrupt and another man finds his own merchandise intact with him, he has more right to it.”

Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Mansur narrated to us, from Rib‘i ibn Hirash, that Hudhayfah told them the Messenger of Allah said: “The angels received the soul of a man from those before you and asked, ‘Did you do any good?’ He said, ‘No.’ They said, ‘Remember.’ He said, ‘I used to give people loans and instruct my servants to give respite to the one in hardship and to be lenient with the one able to pay.’ Allah, Mighty and Sublime, said: ‘Be lenient with him.’”

‘Ali ibn Hujr and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Hujr’s. They said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Nu‘aym ibn Abi Hind, from Rib‘i ibn Hirash, who said: Hudhayfah and Abu Mas‘ud met. Hudhayfah said: “A man met his Lord, and He asked, ‘What did you do?’ He said, ‘I did no good except that I was a wealthy man and collected debts from people. I accepted what was readily paid and gave respite to those in hardship.’ He said: ‘Pardon My servant.’” Abu Mas‘ud said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah say this.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Rib‘i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet: “A man died and entered Paradise. He was asked, ‘What did you used to do?’ He remembered—or was reminded—and said, ‘I traded with people and gave respite to those in hardship, and I was lenient in collecting payment or accepting the currency.’ He was forgiven.” Abu Mas‘ud said: I also heard it from the Messenger of Allah.

Abu Sa‘id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Sa‘d ibn Tariq, from Rib‘i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who said: “A servant of Allah was brought before Allah, who had given him wealth. He asked, ‘What did you do in the world?’—and they conceal nothing from Allah. He said, ‘My Lord, You gave me wealth, and I traded with people. It was my nature to be lenient: I made things easy for those with means and gave respite to those in hardship.’ Allah said: ‘I have more right to do that than you. Pardon My servant.’” ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir al-Juhani and Abu Mas‘ud al-Ansari said: We heard this from the Messenger of Allah.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya’s. Yahya said: Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us; the others said: Abu Mu‘awiyah narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Shaqiq, from Abu Mas‘ud, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “A man from those before you was called to account, and no good was found for him except that he mixed with people and was wealthy, and he instructed his servants to be lenient with those in hardship. Allah, Mighty and Sublime, said: ‘We have more right to do that than he does. Pardon him.’”
